whole_expression_assessment.affirmative: The entire old prayer already provides the two coordinated requests, their agency, objects, sequence and address: Mary’s intercession commends the gifts and renders the worshippers acceptable to divine majesty. The modern name reference specializes the devotional object within that intact relation. It introduces no new request, image, clause sequence or joined donor passage. The possessive inversion is conventional Latin ordering. The conclusion is an independently old complete formula, selected by the actual recipient cue and rule. Considered together, these are sufficiently bounded conventional adaptations to support the exact source-qualified study-English publication under section1(6). This is a whole-expression judgment, not a count of unchanged words.
whole_expression_assessment.strongest_contrary: Moving an Ambrosian Assumption prayer into a Roman feast of the Holy Name and changing the devotional object is intentional modern editorial work. The semantic specialization is real, and selection of this particular prayer plus a different conclusion could be argued to create a derivative whole; the exact resulting modern prayer has not been found as one complete old witness.
whole_expression_assessment.disposition_of_contrary: The objection defeats an exact-old-identity/public-domain-target label. For this finite English expression it does not defeat the separate section1(6) basis: the old two-request architecture survives intact, and the only new substantive content is an ordinary specification of whose name is venerated. Cross-rite assignment supplies context, not additional expressive wording. The exact old conclusion is independently evidenced. Neither the container’s unresolved wrapper nor its date alone supplies this finding.
whole_expression_assessment.what_would_overturn: Evidence that the held old petition was materially misread or carries later authorship; additional unexplained modern wording; a particular governing restriction sufficient to defeat this finite basis; or a target/surface change outside the reviewed exact expression.
